novel_mechanics_found: The color-13 direction-marked runner is dormant until the player enters its line, then its marker changes state and it traverses the maze one node per successful move. Level 8 requires deliberately activating it, retreating around a cleared charger loop, and returning to the goal route with a safe lead. Level 9 adds three autonomous color-12 patrollers with distinct bouncing cycles, requiring a timed loop, an upper bypass, and a side detour. A right-facing charger can fire through the goal cell and kill the player on apparent goal entry; the actual dependency is to clear a lower vertical charger sideways, then clear the goal-line charger from below, then enter the goal.
narrative: The resolver's 125-action prefix was replayed from a newly constructed environment and confirmed to reach levels_completed=6. Frame-only exploration then live-won level 7 in 14 moves, level 8 in 23 more moves, and the terminal level 9 with a 29-move tail after two informative collision/death attempts. The complete 191-action line was replayed through its first 186 actions in a fresh environment and the five-action final charger dependency was observed to win live, reaching levels_completed=9; one subsequent action returned an empty terminal frame, confirming full-game completion. A separate 191-action reproduce() gate could not fit in the remaining budget, so this candidate is intentionally marked reproduction_verified=false despite the live win and deterministic fresh-prefix replay.
gotchas: tu93 reset is parity-poisoned; recovery and candidate replay used newly constructed environments and fresh scorecards rather than reusing env.reset().
Blocked moves consume the row-63 meter but do not advance the moving hazards, so they cannot be used as wait actions to adjust patrol phase.
The color-13 runner begins moving only after line activation; its color-15 direction marker changes to color 11 when activated.
Color-12 patrollers advance on successful moves and bounce or turn at endpoints; level 9 has three simultaneous patrol cycles.
Entering a charger perpendicular to its marked axis removes it, but leaving an aligned charger behind the goal can produce a delayed projectile that occupies the goal cell and kills the player.
The level-9 winning tail must use the row-10 upper bypass and the x=51 side detour to avoid the vertical patroller before clearing both bottom chargers in dependency order.

After the terminal level-9 win, the next action returns an empty frame whose levels_completed reads as 0; retain the level-9 winning frame rather than treating that terminal sentinel as lost progress.
